common.challenges: Challenges and how I solved them

cashtrail.title: CashTrail
cashtrail.subtitle: Personal finance platform that connects accounts, cards, debts and investments without counting the same money twice.
cashtrail.role: Solo project: product, architecture, backend, frontend, tests, CI/CD and Azure infrastructure.
cashtrail.demoHours: Demo available from 6 a.m. to 11 p.m. (Brasília time, UTC−3)
cashtrail.problem: Personal finances are spread across accounts, cards with different billing cycles, fixed bills, debts, investments and income tax. Common tools record expenses but don't connect these parts: the card bill payment counts as an expense on top of the purchases, debts are left out of net worth and investments are recorded as spending.

solution.text: A "personal ERP": each entry feeds the monthly result, the bills to pay, the cash flow and the net worth, with no double counting. I use CashTrail with my own data, and in the public demo each visitor only sees the data they created.

features.records: Accounts, categories and transactions, with CSV bank statement import
features.planning: Budgets, savings goals and recurring entries
features.credit: Cards with billing cycles, installments and debts (Price and SAC schedules)
features.reports: Accrual income statement, cash flow and net worth
features.investments: Investments with automatic quotes and income tax support

architecture.text: The browser loads a static Next.js site served by nginx and calls the FastAPI API directly over REST. The API writes to PostgreSQL through SQLAlchemy and runs scheduled jobs in the same process. Everything runs on Azure, and GitHub Actions builds the images and deploys them.
architecture.slices: The backend is organized in vertical slices: one folder per feature, with routes, rules, persistence and tests. The transactions slice is the core: other slices depend on it, and it depends on none of them. The frontend mirrors the same structure.

browser.title: Browser
browser.text: Loads the site and calls the API

frontend.title: Frontend
frontend.text: Container App: nginx serving the static Next.js site

external.title: External services
external.text: brapi.dev (quotes), Banco Central (indices), Azure Communication Services (email)

deploy.title: CI/CD

decisions.allAdrs: See all decisions (ADRs) in the repository

slices.title: Vertical slices instead of global layers
slices.why: A change usually stays in a single folder, and each feature is tested in isolation.
slices.cost: Small helpers are duplicated on purpose, to avoid coupling slices over a few lines of code.

scheduler.title: APScheduler instead of Celery + Redis
scheduler.why: There was a single periodic job. Celery and Redis would be two more services to maintain, test and pay for on Azure.
scheduler.cost: The scheduler only runs while the container is up. That is why jobs also run at startup.

tokens.title: Refresh token in an httpOnly cookie, access token in memory
tokens.why: In localStorage, any JavaScript on the page could read the tokens, and an XSS flaw would expose them.
tokens.cost: It requires CORS with credentials, CSRF defenses and the frontend and backend on the same site.

transfers.title: Transfers as their own concept
transfers.why: Paying the card bill is not an expense: the purchases were already counted. A new transaction type would force every report to filter it out.
transfers.cost: An account balance now adds up two sources: transactions and transfers.

staticWebApps.title: Azure blocked the hosting plan
staticWebApps.problem: The plan was to host the frontend on Azure Static Web Apps. Creating the resource failed with RequestDisallowedByAzure: the Azure for Students subscription policy blocks this resource type in the region.
staticWebApps.solution: I exported Next.js as a static site and served it with nginx on Container Apps, the same resource type as the backend. Both now deploy the same way. In exchange, I gave up the Next.js server features.

utcDates.title: Dates one day ahead at night
utcDates.problem: After 9 p.m., forms suggested the next day's date. The default date was computed in UTC, three hours ahead of Brasília.
utcDates.solution: I fixed the default date of the forms.

dreComparison.title: An unfair comparison in the income statement
dreComparison.problem: The "previous period" of the income statement compared a partial month with a full month.
dreComparison.solution: The comparison now uses full months on both sides: October with September.

balanceChart.title: A chart that showed the wrong thing
balanceChart.problem: The "Balance over time" chart showed the cumulative result, not the balance.
balanceChart.solution: I removed the chart from the summary. The calendar on the home screen shows the real balance.

items.production: In production on Azure since September 2026, with a public demo.
items.milestones: 16 milestones delivered between September and October 2026, from discovery to redesign.
items.cicd: CI/CD with GitHub Actions: tests, image builds and automated deployment.
items.quality: Decisions documented in ADRs and tests with pytest, Testcontainers and Playwright.

items.timezones: Handle time zones from the very first form: a UTC date looks right until 9 p.m.
items.charts: Check every chart against real data before shipping: one of them showed the cumulative result as if it were the balance.
items.cloudLimits: Test the cloud subscription's restrictions early: the Static Web Apps block only showed up when creating the resource.

coremanager.title: CoreManager
coremanager.subtitle: Inventory management system that started as a school capstone, was bought by a company and went through a full refactoring, with tests and a security audit.
coremanager.role: Group capstone in which I was responsible for development. I did the 12-stage refactoring and the security audit on my own. Maintenance and support are handled by the group.
coremanager.docs: See the documentation in the repository
coremanager.problem: A company needed to control its inventory: register products and suppliers, record stock entries and exits and generate reports. After the sale, a second problem showed up: the capstone code worked, but it had dead code, no automated tests and security flaws, such as missing CSRF protection.

solution.text: A web system in framework-free PHP, with MySQL or MariaDB. After the sale, I refactored the code in 12 stages. Each stage had its own branch and was only merged into main after the automated tests and a manual test script.

features.catalog: Products and suppliers, with address lookup through ViaCEP
features.movements: Stock entries and exits, with history
features.reports: Financial and stock reports, in PDF and Excel
features.users: Users with an administrator or employee role

architecture.text: A PHP 8.2 monolith with a single entry point, public/index.php. Each request goes through the router, the login and administrator middlewares and the CSRF check before reaching the controller. The controller calls a use case or a model, which talks to the database.
architecture.slices: The backend has 7 slices: Authentication, Dashboard, Products, Stock movements, Reports, Users and Suppliers. Only the owning slice writes to its own table; the others just read. Business rules live in PHP. The database holds simple constraints (CHECK, UNIQUE and FK) and a stock audit trigger.
architecture.diagramLabel: Diagram of a request's path in CoreManager

browser.title: Browser
browser.text: Server-rendered pages and actions with fetch and JSON

entry.title: Apache and router
entry.text: public/index.php is the only folder served; an unknown route returns 404

guards.title: Middlewares and CSRF
guards.text: Login, administrator permission and a CSRF token on every non-GET request

controller.title: Controller
controller.text: Reads the input and responds with HTML, JSON or a redirect

slices.title: Vertical slices in framework-free PHP
slices.text: Each feature uses the same name in the backend, the views and the JavaScript. There are three folder trees instead of one because, without a build step, the browser can only reach the public/ folder.

useCases.title: A use case only when there is a business rule
useCases.text: Simple CRUD stays in the controller and the model. A use case file only exists for rules, transactions or calculations, such as recording a stock movement.

response.title: A single JSON response contract
response.text: Every JSON response has the same four fields: sucesso, mensagem, dados and requer_confirmacao. Controllers build the response through a single method.

escaping.title: Store as typed, escape on output
escaping.text: Data is stored exactly as typed. Escaping happens when it is displayed, with htmlspecialchars() in PHP and textContent in JavaScript.

productHistory.title: History depended on the product name
productHistory.problem: Stock movements stored the product name, so renaming a product affected its history.
productHistory.solution: Movements now reference the product id. Renaming keeps the history.

sessions.title: Sessions that did not follow the account
sessions.problem: The audit showed that account changes did not apply to sessions that were already open.
sessions.solution: Every request checks the user in the database. Changing the password ends the other sessions, and a session expires after 2 hours of inactivity or 12 hours after login.

loginLimit.title: Login with no attempt limit
loginLimit.problem: The assessment recorded 21 wrong passwords in a row with no lockout.
loginLimit.solution: Attempt limits per account and per IP, with a 15-minute lockout. The response time is the same when the account does not exist.

csrfXss.title: Forms without CSRF protection and XSS on the dashboard
csrfXss.problem: POST and DELETE actions had no CSRF token, and the dashboard had an XSS flaw.
csrfXss.solution: A CSRF token on every POST and DELETE, checked in a single place, before the controllers. The XSS flaw was fixed with output escaping.

items.production: Bought by a company and in production since 2025.
items.refactor: Refactoring completed in 12 stages, with about 2,800 lines of dead code removed.
items.tests: 66 PHPUnit tests and 70 E2E tests with Playwright, running on MariaDB 10.4 and MySQL 8.0.
items.security: Security audit with fixes to sessions, login, CSRF and input validation.

items.testsFirst: Write the tests before changing the structure: they came in stage 5, and the move to slices only in stage 9.
items.ids: Link records by id, never by name.
items.audit: Security needs its own audit: the system worked, and the login still accepted unlimited attempts.
